newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: City of Prague approves intl bond issue.
newsitem.headline: City of Prague approves intl bond issue.

text.p: The City of Prague assembly approved a plan on Friday to issue an international bond of up to nine billion crowns ($279.2 million), city officials said.
The assembly approved the plan on condition that the issue would have a maturity of either five, seven or 10 years, depending on market conditions.
City officials have said they would like to launch the bond sometime before the end of the year.
But the assembly still has to decide in which currency it will issue the bonds.
Six billion crowns of the money raised will be used for infrastructure projects. The remainder will be kept in a housing fund.
"Three billion crowns of this will be money that will not enter circulation," said Prague Mayor Jan Koukal.
Both the government and central bank have criticised the idea of Prague's issuing a bond, given the government's current battle to restrict demand and keep spending in line.
The Finance Ministry has final approval of any bond issue by a municipality.
Koukal said funds from the issue would not be thrown "all at once" into the economy and that the Finance Ministry had given a preliminary positive stance on the issue.
But a senior ministry official, who asked not to be named, said the ministry could set unattainable conditions for issuance of the bonds if it wants to stop it.

The Czech economy was shaken in late May by a speculative attack on the crown that forced the central bank to float the currency. As a result, the crown fell to more than 15 percent below its highs against the dollar and mark in early February.

The currency's controlled float was backed by a rise in key interest rates and a government austerity package aimed to slow domestic demand and dampen inflationary effects from the crown's depreciation.
Prague carries an indicative investment-grade "A" rating from Standard & Poor's, the same as the Czech sovereign debt.
